alt: Farah shows Mirza two forecasting paths on the bridge before their next comparison.
prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit. Recompose the LAST reference into a 1536x1024 landscape Deep Orbit lesson scene. References 1 through 2 are canonical identity authorities in this order: commander-mirza, dr-farah. Reference 3 is the room authority; reference 4 is the original edit target for story action, lighting and palette only. Preserve exact recognizable canonical facial structure, eye spacing, nose, jaw, mouth, complexion, age and signature equipment. Exactly 2 humans, the named cast only. Preserve balanced adult proportions and candid expressions. Exactly two complete arms per person, each from its own shoulder through one elbow and neutral wrist to one plausible hand. Ordinary thumb sides, fingers and natural object contact; no extra arm or bent prop. No camera-facing portraits. Faces visible naturally three-quarter with eyes directed toward work or each other. Use available empty wall or upper space for a large upright primary lesson display that is physically plausible and faces its operators. All text and lines follow the display plane, crisp and generously sized with comfortable margins. Keep essential content fully visible. Never put the sole lesson evidence upside down on paper or flat table, or on a tiny tabletop screen beneath a blank wall. Secondary paper can face its owner, but essential content is repeated upright. Remove meaningless decorative technical labels. No generic success verdicts, invented numbers, speech bubbles, watermarks or signatures. Commander Mirza: dark-skinned mature woman, close-cropped dark hair with gray temples, gold-trim dark command uniform, round chest badge and small hoop earrings. Dr. Farah: medium-brown skin, dark tied hair, gray lab coat, earrings and translucent green AR lens over her left eye.
Specific action and staging: Commander Mirza and Farah stand around the bridge table in a candid discussion. Mirza listens with a searching raised eyebrow and one hand resting on the rail; Farah uses a simple trackball while explaining, other hand relaxed on table. Both recognizable faces are visible, eyes on each other or the shared upright screen. Recompose the previous flat upside-down table comparison onto a large upright bridge panel.
Exact visible display content: Title: "Two forecast runs". Two clean paths: "Recent window" to "Forecast" to "Feed back prediction" with loop. Add a clear note above the rollout path "Start from observed history". Once predictions feed back, the window is no longer exclusively observed history; and "Observed history" to "One-step prediction" to "Add next observation" with loop. Label first path "Rollout" and second "Replay". Footer "Compare with readings that arrive". This is a setup, with no invented results or success.

ownReview.method: Fresh original-resolution image, native face crops compared with canonical portraits, and hand/prop crops. Complete arm chains, body support, gaze, reader/operator direction, surface perspective and current lesson values inspected.
ownReview.action: Farah operates the table trackball while briefing Mirza, who rests one arm over the rail and one hand on the table.
ownReview.emotion: Engaged explanation and thoughtful command attention.
ownReview.eyeline: Farah and Mirza look at each other beside the two-run comparison.
ownReview.narrativeReason: The briefing distinguishes a rollout that feeds predictions back from one-step replay with new observations.
findings: The revised diagram labels the rollout input Recent window, explicitly starts from observed history and states that feedback makes it no longer exclusively observed history.
